units.text: UI tests in Compose use *semantics* to interact with the UI hierarchy. The *semantics tree* is generated alongside the UI hierarchy and describes the hierarchy.

quotes.quote: UI tests in Compose use *semantics* to interact with the UI hierarchy.
is generated alongside the UI hierarchy and describes the hierarchy.

units.text: The semantics framework is primarily used for accessibility, so tests take advantage of the information exposed by semantics about the UI hierarchy. Developers decide what and how much to expose.

quotes.quote: The semantics framework is primarily used for accessibility, so tests take advantage of the information exposed by semantics about the UI hierarchy. Developers decide what and how much to expose.

units.text: Testing a Compose UI is different from testing a view-based UI. In Compose, because only some composables *emit* UI into the UI hierarchy, you need a different approach to matching UI elements.

quotes.quote: Testing a Compose UI is different from testing a view-based UI.
In Compose, because only some composables *emit* UI into the UI hierarchy, you need a different approach to matching UI elements.

units.text: Given a button that consists of an icon and a text element, the default semantics tree only contains the text label "Like". This is because some composables, such as `Text`, already expose some properties to the semantics tree. You can add properties to the semantics tree by using a `Modifier`.

quotes.quote: the default semantics tree only contains the text label "Like".
This is because some composables, such as `Text`, already expose some properties to the semantics tree. You can add properties to the semantics tree by using a `Modifier`.
modifier = Modifier.semantics { contentDescription = "Add to favorites" }

units.text: Finders let you select one or multiple elements (or *nodes* in the semantics tree) to make assertions or perform actions on them.

quotes.quote: Finders let you select one or multiple elements (or *nodes* in the semantics tree) to make assertions or perform actions on them.

units.text: Some of these APIs accept a `SemanticsMatcher` to refer to one or more *nodes* in the semantics tree.

quotes.quote: Some of these APIs accept a `SemanticsMatcher` to refer to one or more *nodes* in the semantics tree.

units.text: By default, composables are accessible from UiAutomator only by their convenient descriptors (displayed text, content description, etc.). If you want to access any composable that uses `Modifier.testTag`, you need to enable the semantic property `testTagsAsResourceId` for the particular composable's subtree.

quotes.quote: By default, composables are accessible from UiAutomator only by their convenient descriptors (displayed text, content description, etc.).
you need to enable the semantic property testTagsAsResourceId for the particular composable's subtree.

units.text: Enable the semantic property only once high in your composables hierarchy to ensure all nested composables with `Modifier.testTag` are accessible from UiAutomator.

quotes.quote: Enable the semantic property only once high in your composables hierarchy to ensure all nested composables with Modifier.testTag are accessible from UiAutomator.

Scaffold( // Enables for all composables in the hierarchy. modifier = Modifier.semantics { testTagsAsResourceId = true } ){ // Modifier.testTag is accessible from UiAutomator for composables nested here. LazyColumn( modifier = Modifier.testTag("myLazyColumn") ){ // Content } }

units.text: You can create custom semantics properties to expose information to tests. To do this, define a new `SemanticsPropertyKey` and make it available using the `SemanticsPropertyReceiver`.

quotes.quote: to expose information to tests. To do this, define a new SemanticsPropertyKey and make it available using the SemanticsPropertyReceiver.
// Creates a semantics property of type Long. val PickedDateKey = SemanticsPropertyKey<Long>("PickedDate") var SemanticsPropertyReceiver.pickedDate by PickedDateKey

units.text: Now use that property in the `semantics` modifier:

quotes.quote: Now use that property in the semantics modifier:
val datePickerValue by remember { mutableStateOf(0L) } MyCustomDatePicker( modifier = Modifier.semantics { pickedDate = datePickerValue } )

units.text: When migrating complex UIs to Compose, you might encounter identical Compose elements nested inside multiple traditional Android Views---such as within a `RecyclerView` or a `ViewPager`. In these scenarios, a standard Compose search like `onNodeWithText("Save")` might fail with a "Multiple nodes found" error.

quotes.quote: When migrating complex UIs to Compose, you might encounter identical Compose elements nested inside multiple traditional Android Views---such as within a RecyclerView or a ViewPager. In these scenarios, a standard Compose search like onNodeWithText("Save") might fail with a "Multiple nodes found" error.

units.text: Use the `onRootWithViewInteraction` API on your test rule. This function accepts an Espresso `ViewInteraction`, allowing you to leverage Espresso to isolate a specific container View and perform Compose interactions exclusively within that scoped hierarchy.

quotes.quote: Use the onRootWithViewInteraction API on your test rule. This function accepts an Espresso ViewInteraction, allowing you to leverage Espresso to isolate a specific container View and perform Compose interactions exclusively within that scoped hierarchy.

units.text: This API is specifically designed for testing Compose components nested inside Views. To test Views nested inside Compose, continue using standard Espresso interactions.

quotes.quote: This API is specifically designed for testing Compose components nested inside Views. To test Views nested inside Compose, continue using standard Espresso interactions.

units.text:
// Select the "Header" View container
val headerInteraction = onView(withId(header_id))

// Scope the Compose interaction to only the Header
composeTestRule
    .onRootWithViewInteraction(headerInteraction)
    .onNodeWithContentDescription("Settings")
    .performClick()

quotes.quote: // Select the "Header" View container val headerInteraction = onView(withId(header_id)) // Scope the Compose interaction to only the Header composeTestRule .onRootWithViewInteraction(headerInteraction) .onNodeWithContentDescription("Settings") .performClick()
